title: Finite Q3 source-boundary quadratic Duhamel norm envelope and cutoff stress
question: Does source-boundary commutation give a finite quadratic-time action bound, and do the resulting norm constants remain controlled when the path volume and oscillator cutoff are varied?
method: Construct the canonical Q3 Hamiltonians on path2, path3 and path4 for oscillator dimensions 2 and 3 with chi=1, r=-1, g=3/5, c=3/5 and lambda=1/10.

For each nested pair embed the smaller Hamiltonian and source q/p character with an identity tensor factor, form Delta=H_large-(H_small tensor I), and verify the exact finite source-boundary commutator is below the declared numerical floor.

Apply the finite Duhamel identity and the conservative induced-norm consequence ||alpha_t^large(A)-alpha_t^small(A)|| <= min(2||A||,2||Delta||( ||H0||+||Delta|| )||A||t^2/hbar^2). Check the envelope at five declared real times and retain the exact H0 and Delta norms.
Record nested commutator onset through order five as a causal graph-distance lower-bound diagnostic, without asserting an exact order when the finite cutoff censors it.
Run a non-importing independent reconstruction, compare all rows and derived fields, compile and registry-check Lean R343, and enforce the downstream QFT scope firewall.
finding: The primary lane passes 71/71 assertions and the non-importing independent lane passes 72/72; the integrated verifier passes 26/26 with Lean R343 PASS. The largest source-boundary tangent commutator is 2.775557561562892e-16. The conservative finite quadratic envelope contains every direct action defect; the largest direct operator-norm defect is 0.007178528437484149 and the maximum defect-to-envelope ratio is 0.0035892642187420726. The exact finite norm rows show Delta norms 0.6875 for oscillator dimension 2 and 2.32007703464569 for dimension 3, while the embedded H0 norm rises from 0.7249999999999999 to 4.69935615336013 across the tested path pairs and cutoff. Observed first nonzero orders are [4,3] for path2->path3 at dimension 3 and [-1,5] for path3->path4; -1 denotes no order above the witness floor within the declared order-five cutoff.
decision_reason: The finite Duhamel identity plus source commutation yields a valid, deliberately conservative quadratic-time norm envelope. It exposes the global Hamiltonian-norm dependence that must be replaced by a local energy or modular estimate before a thermodynamic QFT argument can close. The cutoff/volume rows are finite stress evidence, not a proof of divergence or a no-go theorem.

adversarial_review.check: All action defects and bounds use the induced operator norm; no Frobenius norm is substituted for the stated envelope.
The exact Delta/source commutator is checked before the quadratic envelope is applied; floating residuals are retained in the run JSON.
The coefficient is the conservative 2||Delta||( ||H0||+||Delta|| )||A||/hbar^2 obtained from Duhamel and commutator norm inequalities; it is not fitted to observed defects.
The min with 2||A|| uses finite unitary-action isometry and is retained only as a second finite bound, not as a decay assertion.
Higher-than-minimal first nonzero commutator orders or censored orders are recorded as cancellation/cutoff data, while only the graph-distance lower bound is enforced.
Oscillator dimensions 2 and 3 are separate finite fixtures; their norm growth is not promoted to an unbounded-operator theorem.
Only path2, path3 and path4 are tested, and exact H0/Delta norms are reported; no volume-uniform extrapolation is made.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator matrices, Q3 terms, embeddings, actions and envelopes without importing the primary lane.
R343 certifies only the finite associative commutator decomposition; the norm inequality and all numerical values remain finite Python evidence.

A finite norm envelope with explicit global-norm dependence does not prove a common OS carrier, uniform D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, Hamiltonian-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

next_action: Replace the global norm coefficient by a local energy- or modular-weighted bound on the unbounded Q3 core, and test whether a source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform coefficient can be proved. If not, register the exact failure boundary.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite nested Q3 source-boundary norm-envelope checkpoint. It is not a thermodynamic common-Hilbert theorem, a common-alpha construction, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, or a QFT/Clay closure.

It does not prove or refute another common OS carrier, uniform source-boundary decay, direct Cauchy convergence, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, a GNS gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
